question: What does verse 72 teach?
premises: Even a minister who is a limb of the king is ruined if he harms the king.
The reversal is not to be taken in the same way.
One should resort to the upward view.
inference: Harm to the source of authority ruins the dependent; the proper reversal is to adopt the upward view.
uncertainties: The exact scope of "netyevamūrdhvāṃ" is ambiguous between negating the reversal and directing resort to the upward view.
The precise relation to the previous verse's downward/upward imagery is not fully explicit.
plain_english: Even a minister, though a limb of the king, is ruined if he harms the king; but the reversal is not the same—one should resort to the upward view.
